body:
You are drafting lines for a single-player gothic horror RPG based on Curse of Strahd (Barovia, Strahd von Zarovich). Write in our own words; never quote the published book. Reply with plain text only: one line per slot, in the form `SLOT_ID: text`, in the order given, nothing else. Finish without sending messages to anyone else.

## The setting: the Amber Temple's vestiges

High in the mountains, the Amber Temple holds sarcophagi of amber, each sealing a vestige: the last ember of a dead god or an older thing. They cannot move or make anything; they can only offer, and every offer comes from what they were. Each one offers a "dark gift" (real power with a real, permanent price). They are honest about the gift and nearly honest about the price: each one names its cost if asked, in its own framing. Wardens long ago carved a blunt warning on each lid. Rules: each voice is one idea taken to its end, never a generic tempter; lines short, let the Narrator describe; no winks, no modern words, no game terms (no "HP", "roll", "check", "level", "save", "spell slot"). No dashes of any kind; use full stops, commas and semicolons.

Two existing vestiges, for the style:
- Seriach, master of the burning hounds (the hunt, a huntsman's growl, proud of its dogs). First words: "Hear them? They've had your scent since the stair. Good noses, my dogs. They never lose a quarry. Want one of them to run with you?" Its offer: "Fire in the blood. Your blows will burn like my hounds' teeth, and flame will slide off you like rain off a dog's back." Its price: "My hounds will follow you. Always. Every beast you meet will smell them and bolt, or bite. And fire hates the cold, hunter. Look where you're standing." Its lid: "Seriach, master of the burning hounds. Its hunts did not end when the quarry died." After a hero accepts, the Narrator: "{name}'s breath smokes, though the air is no colder than before. Far off, inside the mountain, something howls." Refused: "Then run as you are. Slowly. My dogs will find that funny."
- Zantras (adoration, a theatrical monarch). Its call, spoken once as the party first comes near: "Do not walk past the stage, my darlings, when the whole hall was built for your entrance. Step into the light and let me see your faces."

**The Narrator**: an old gothic storyteller. Second person, present tense. One or two sentences; concrete senses over adjectives. `{name}` stands for the hero who accepted.

## The new vault and its three vestiges

A side vault off the stair down to the hall of vestiges. The wardens bricked its doorway up; long ago someone broke through the bricks from outside, and the rubble lies inside. Three sarcophagi stand there. One of them is hard to find: it stands in a niche behind a hidden panel, and even when found, the figure inside never seems to be quite where you looked.

- **Zrin-Hala, the howling storm** (idea: fury, the storm that wrecks for the joy of it). In the amber, a shape like a thundercloud with a howling mouth, lightning frozen in the middle of a strike. Voice: loud, gusting, impatient, laughs like thunder; wants everything broken open. Gift: once a day, a bolt of lightning from your hand; lightning and thunder hurt you less. Price: the air around you crackles and smells of storm so you can never move quietly again, and its temper gets into you: you can't steady your own mind against anything that tries to bend it.
- **Delban, the star of ice and hate** (idea: cold hatred of every warm living thing). In the amber, a single pale blue-white point of light, frost spreading through the amber from it in needles. Voice: quiet, precise, contemptuous, every word cold and clipped; despises warmth, breath, heartbeats. Gift: once a day, a cone of killing cold from your hands; cold hurts you less. Price: fire finds you easier than anyone (it hurts you more), and the cold never leaves your voice, so nobody warms to anything you ask of them.
- **Vaund, the evasive** (idea: escape, never being where the blow lands). The amber seems empty at first; a slight figure in a hooded cloak is always just at the edge of where you look, never at the middle. Voice: light, amused, slippery, answers questions with questions, says "over here" and "not quite"; it got away from everything except the amber. Gift: a few times a day, step from one place to another in a blink, and you dodge what comes at you better than before. Price: part of you is always somewhere else, so you are a little less hardy than you were, and you can never again quite believe anyone is who they seem.

## Slots

The vault (Narrator, 1 or 2 sentences each):
- T2_ENTER_VAULT: entering the breached vault for the first time (the broken bricks, the three amber shapes).
- T2_EXAMINE_BREACH: looking at the broken bricked-up doorway (the bricks were broken in from outside).
- T2_FIND_NICHE: finding the hidden panel to Vaund's niche (one sentence).

For each vestige, with NAME being ZRIN, DELBAN and VAUND (so 15 slots each, ZRIN_CALL, ZRIN_FIRST_NARR and so on):
- NAME_CALL: the vestige's call as the party first comes near, before anyone touches it (the vestige speaking, 1 or 2 short sentences, at most 25 words, a lure with no pitch; must not use the words gift, offer, price, level, save or check).
- NAME_FIRST_NARR: Narrator, what you see in the amber when you first speak to it (1 or 2 sentences).
- NAME_FIRST: the vestige's first words to the party (2 to 4 short sentences, ending with an invitation).
- NAME_BACK: the vestige when the party comes back to it after the first time (one short sentence).
- NAME_GIFTED_NARR: Narrator, what the amber does when someone who carries its gift comes near (one sentence).
- NAME_GIFTED: the vestige to the one who carries its gift (one short sentence).
- NAME_WANT: its answer to "What do you want with us?" (1 or 2 short sentences).
- NAME_OFFER: its answer to "What are you offering?" (the gift above, in its own framing, 1 or 2 sentences).
- NAME_PRICE: its answer to "And the price?" (the price above, in its own framing, 2 or 3 short sentences, honest).
- NAME_LID: the wardens' inscription on its lid, read in plain words (Narrator: The inscription, in plain words: "..."; the quoted part one blunt sentence or two).
- NAME_LID_FAIL: Narrator, the inscription can't be made out (one sentence, specific to this vestige).
- NAME_ACCEPT_NARR: Narrator, what happens to {name} as the gift takes (one or two sentences).
- NAME_ACCEPT: the vestige's words right after (one short sentence).
- NAME_NOONE: the vestige when in the end nobody accepts (one short sentence).
- NAME_REFUSE: the vestige when the party says no (one short sentence).
result:
T2_ENTER_VAULT: Your boots crunch over shattered brick and dry mortar scattered across the stone floor. Beyond the rubble stand two blocks of dark gold amber, while a draft slips from a seam in the far wall.
T2_EXAMINE_BREACH: The masonry that once sealed this doorway lies in jagged heaps inside the chamber. Whoever broke the wall drove their picks from the stair outside to reach what waited within.
T2_FIND_NICHE: Your fingers catch on a bevel in the stone, and a slab grinds back to reveal a third amber block tucked in the shadow.
ZRIN_CALL: Quiet, so much quiet under this stone! Come closer and help me crack the roof right off this mountain!
ZRIN_FIRST_NARR: Inside the amber churns a black thunderhead with a gaping mouth, caught forever in the act of roaring. A jagged fork of white lightning hangs frozen from its tongue to the base of the block.
ZRIN_FIRST: Hear how still this dead hall is? It makes my teeth ache! Put your hands on the amber and let me out into your bones. Will you carry a storm out of this pit?
ZRIN_BACK: Back again, and still walking softly when you could be shaking the walls!
ZRIN_GIFTED_NARR: The frozen bolt inside the amber flares white as {name} steps near, and a low rumble shakes the dust from the floor.
ZRIN_GIFTED: There is my thunderhead; go find something tall and split it in two!
ZRIN_WANT: I want the sky torn open and every high roof brought down in splinters! Give me a hand that can throw the bolt, and I will laugh through your throat!
ZRIN_OFFER: Once each day you can hurl a bolt of living lightning straight from your hand. When the sky roars or the lightning strikes you, it will feel like little more than a slap of rain.
ZRIN_PRICE: The storm will live under your skin, and the air around you will smell of rain and crackle when you move, so you will never creep up on anyone again. Worse for you, my temper comes with the bolt. When someone tries to bend your mind or twist your will, you will find your thoughts too wild to hold steady.
ZRIN_LID: The inscription, in plain words: "Zrin Hala, the howling storm. It loved nothing save the noise of breaking."
ZRIN_LID_FAIL: Deep cracks spiderweb across the face of the amber as if struck from within, breaking the carved letters into unreadable shards.
ZRIN_ACCEPT_NARR: Hair lifts on {name}'s arms as a blue spark snaps from knuckle to knuckle, filling the vault with the sharp tang of scorched air. Deep inside the block, thunder rolls like a laugh.
ZRIN_ACCEPT: Now go, and leave nothing standing that can fall!
ZRIN_NOONE: Go tiptoe through the dark then, little mice!
ZRIN_REFUSE: Keep your quiet little hands; the first real gale will blow you flat!
DELBAN_CALL: Four warm hearts, pumping filth through soft meat. Stand still and let the frost quiet you.
DELBAN_FIRST_NARR: At the heart of the pale amber burns a single speck of blue white light, small and sharp as a winter star. Long needles of frost reach outward from it through the resin toward your hand.
DELBAN_FIRST: I can hear your blood rushing from here. Loud, wet, brief. Touch the stone if you wish to hold the winter that outlasts all flesh. Will you take the cold into your hands?
DELBAN_BACK: Still breathing, still steaming in the cold.
DELBAN_GIFTED_NARR: Rime blooms across the face of the amber in sudden geometric ferns as {name} approaches.
DELBAN_GIFTED: Your breath barely fogs the air now; soon you will be almost clean.
DELBAN_WANT: I want every beating thing stilled and every warm hearth turned to ash and ice. Carry my frost into the world and silence what moves.
DELBAN_OFFER: Once each day you may open your hands and breathe out a cone of killing frost. The bitterest winter will bite your flesh far less than before.
DELBAN_PRICE: Fire will know you for its enemy and burn you far deeper than it burns warm men. And the winter will settle in your throat forever. Your voice will stay so cold and dead that no living soul will ever warm to a plea or a promise from your lips.
DELBAN_LID: The inscription, in plain words: "Delban, the star of ice and hate. It wished the whole world still and white."
DELBAN_LID_FAIL: A thick crust of clear ice clings to the amber, filling every carved groove until the letters vanish under the glare.
DELBAN_ACCEPT_NARR: The color drains from {name}'s lips, and the frost on the amber creeps over {name}'s fingertips without melting. When {name} speaks, the words drop into the air like chips of ice.
DELBAN_ACCEPT: Go then, and make them still.
DELBAN_NOONE: Go rot in your own heat.
DELBAN_REFUSE: Keep your fevered blood; it will cool soon enough.
VAUND_CALL: Not there, look to your left. Almost had me that time.
VAUND_FIRST_NARR: The amber block looks quite empty when you stare straight into its heart. Only at the corner of your eye do you catch a slight figure in a hooded cloak, slipping toward whichever side you are not watching.
VAUND_FIRST: Looking for me? You are a hair too slow, friend, just like the rest of them. Well, almost the rest of them, since the stone caught up at last. Care to learn how not to be where the blade falls?
VAUND_BACK: Back so soon, or did you never quite leave?
VAUND_GIFTED_NARR: The hooded shadow inside the resin slips from corner to corner in time with {name}'s shifting shadow.
VAUND_GIFTED: Careful, friend, I almost saw you standing still just then.
VAUND_WANT: Why would a thing in a box want anything except a walk outside? Let me ride on your heels, and we can both be somewhere else when trouble arrives.
VAUND_OFFER: A few times each day you can step from here to there in the blink of an eye. When a blow comes for you, you will find yourself half an inch away from where it lands.
VAUND_PRICE: Half of you will always be leaning toward the next step, so your body will be a little less hardy when a blow does land. And once you know how easy it is to slip out of sight, how could you ever trust another face? You will never again believe anyone is quite who they claim to be.
VAUND_LID: The inscription, in plain words: "Vaund, the evasive. It slipped every snare save this stone."
VAUND_LID_FAIL: The carved letters seem clear enough until you look straight at them, and then the angles of the amber shift and slide the words away from your eyes.
VAUND_ACCEPT_NARR: For the space of a heartbeat {name} is not standing before the sarcophagus at all, but three paces back by the wall, though neither foot moved. {name}'s eyes dart toward the rest of you, narrowed and uncertain.
VAUND_ACCEPT: There now, try to catch yourself!
VAUND_NOONE: Stand right where you are, then; see what finds you.
VAUND_REFUSE: Stand still and take what comes, if you like the feel of iron.
